.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Gradually warming temperatures today and Sunday 
with increasing precipitation chances each day. 

Surface high pressure shifts northeast towards New England
today and tomorrow, with gradually warming temperatures
expected. High temperatures will be in the 70s to mid 80s across
the forecast area. Aloft, multiple shortwave troughs track
across the mid-Atlantic, bringing daily precipitation chances 
mainly along and west of the Blue Ridge. Precipitation chances 
increase Sunday, although coverage of showers and thunderstorms 
remains scattered due to weak forcing. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Returning to a summer-like pattern next week.

Beginning of next week, ensemble model guidance supports an UL 
trough continuing to dig in to our region, leading to falling 
heights and increasing chances for showers and t-storms Tuesday 
through Wednesday morning. With Tuesday's dew points in the mid 
70s to upper 60s and high temperatures in the mid 70s west of 
the Blue Ridge and high 80s east of the Blue Ridge, there is 
potential for ample moisture and heat to support showers and 
t-storm development. This coincides with ample instability 
rising into the 1,500 to 2,500 J/kg range. With enough vertical 
shear and height falls, global models support an active day of 
thunderstorm activity. Ensembles show some sagging of the 
surface isobaric pattern with its position indicative of a lee- 
side trough. This will likely be one focus for convection along 
with terrain circulations and the upstream cold front. 

Damaging wind gusts and torrential downpours are possible with any 
such storm. Given the later arrival of the front, the threat for 
storms may persist beyond the core diurnal heating hours. 

Models show this frontal zone sagging southward to near the Virginia-
North Carolina border by mid-week. A shift to post-frontal 
northwesterlies should gradually quell the threat for thunderstorms. 
Dew points begin to fall with temperatures remaining seasonable. 
Tuesday's hot temperatures seem to persist into Wednesday through 
Friday, with high temperatures largely topping out in the upper 80s 
to low 90s which is close to climatology for late July.  Slightly 
lowered dew points allows for Overnight lows fall into the 60s most 
nights. This subtle decrease in humid conditions aids lowering 
precipitation chances to around 20% that could persist through the 
rest of the week.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Primarily VFR conditions are expected today with light winds out
of the east/southeast. Showers are possible on Sunday along the
Blue Ridge with the chance for thunderstorms returning Monday. 
Sub-VFR conditions are possible in precipitation. Easterly winds
today and tomorrow shift to southerly on Monday.

Tuesday is looking like a much more active weather day ahead of a 
notable cold front. Convective-related restrictions become 
increasingly likely, particularly during the afternoon/evening 
hours. Some showers may linger into Wednesday which could be 
accompanied by low ceilings. Gradual improvements take place 
thereafter as winds shift to northwesterly. Before this wind shift 
occurs, expect mainly south to southwesterly winds with afternoon 
gusts to around 15 to 20 knots.

&&

.MARINE...
Light winds are expected today and Sunday with winds remaining
out of the east. No hazardous marine conditions are expected. 

Southerly winds pick up in intensity on Monday evening/night into 
Tuesday. Channeling effects could bring gusts to around 20 knots or 
so, which would be supportive of Small Craft Advisories, 
particularly across wider waters of the Chesapeake Bay. A convective 
threat increases through the day on Tuesday which would support the 
need of some Special Marine Warnings. Winds shift to northwesterly 
by Wednesday with gusts to around 10 to 15 knots.&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies rebound within onshore flow today and Sunday, 
with more sensitive locations potentially reaching Action Stage 
through the weekend. Annapolis could approach minor flood 
thresholds early next week.
